title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: AWS
providers.scope_notes: Covers Amazon Web Services (IAM, STS, IAM Identity Center, IAM Roles Anywhere, Amazon Bedrock). All features are available in every AWS account; SCPs and centralized root access require AWS Organizations, and Control Tower controls require AWS Control Tower.

controls.name: Deactivate / delete access key (UpdateAccessKey, DeleteAccessKey)
controls.what: Setting a key Inactive or deleting it stops all further use of that key.
controls.setting: IAM console > Users > Security credentials > Actions > Deactivate/Delete; API UpdateAccessKey / DeleteAccessKey

controls.name: Service control policy (SCP)
controls.what: An SCP can deny actions such as iam:CreateAccessKey or iam:CreateServiceSpecificCredential for all IAM users and roles in member accounts.
controls.setting: AWS Organizations > Policies > Service control policies

controls.name: aws:SourceIp deny policy
controls.what: Identity policy or SCP that denies any request from outside listed CIDR ranges.
controls.setting: IAM policy / SCP with NotIpAddress aws:SourceIp

controls.name: Time-bound policy (aws:CurrentTime)
controls.what: Inline deny policy that blocks all actions after a set date, giving long-term keys an effective expiry.
controls.setting: IAM > Users > Permissions > Create inline policy

controls.name: IAM Access Analyzer unused access
controls.what: Generates findings for IAM user access keys unused within a set window.
controls.setting: IAM Access Analyzer > Create unused access analyzer

no_control.what: No built-in expiry for IAM user access keys.
sts:GetCallerIdentity cannot be denied, so any valid key can confirm its identity.

controls_unknown: Whether long-term Bedrock API keys can be set to never expire, and their maximum lifetime.
Token format/prefix for Bedrock API keys (not documented on fetched pages).
Which CloudTrail field identifies the specific Bedrock API key on a request (key value is not logged).
Default session duration for IAM Roles Anywhere when durationSeconds is omitted.
Exact CloudTrail eventName strings for CreateAccessKey/UpdateAccessKey/DeleteAccessKey were not shown on fetched pages (they match the IAM API action names, which CloudTrail logs).

authentication.summary: Access key ID (AKIA...) plus secret access key used to SigV4-sign AWS API and CLI requests. Up to two keys per IAM user.

federation.details: Keys belong to IAM users, not to an external IdP. AWS recommends federation with temporary credentials for humans and roles for workloads; no doc states whether IdP sign-in policy applies to these keys (it is not part of the signing flow).

ip_restriction.boundary: Not a setting: an identity policy or SCP that denies requests when aws:SourceIp is outside allowed ranges. It is evaluated on every signed API request. aws:SourceIp is absent for calls through VPC endpoints (use aws:VpcSourceIp) and SCPs do not cover the management account.

lifetime.summary: Never expire; a time-bound deny policy (aws:CurrentTime) can cut them off

renewal.summary: Same key pair is reused until deactivated or deleted; rotation is manual (create second key, switch, deactivate, delete).

administration.summary: Admins with IAM permissions create, deactivate and delete keys; SCPs/IAM policies can deny iam:CreateAccessKey and restrict what the user can call.
administration.conditions: SCPs need AWS Organizations and do not apply to the management account.

sso.details: AWS says IAM user access keys cannot be used with MFA-protected API access, and they are not issued through an IdP.

offboard.details: Access keys belong to the IAM user; deleting the IAM user deletes its keys. IAM users are not tied to IdP/SCIM deprovisioning.

inventory.details: The IAM credential report lists every user in the account with access key status.

inventory.ui: IAM console > Credential report > Download Report
inventory.cli: aws iam generate-credential-report; aws iam get-credential-report

network.ui: IAM console > Users (or Roles) > name > Permissions tab > edit policy > JSON: Deny * with NotIpAddress aws:SourceIp; or AWS Organizations console > Policies > Service control policies > Create policy (Deny * with NotIpAddress aws:SourceIp) > attach to OU/account
network.cli: aws iam put-user-policy (inline deny) or aws organizations create-policy + attach-policy

reads.ui: CloudTrail console > Trails > trail > Data events > Edit > enable S3 data events; then filter trail logs on eventName=GetObject (not in Event history)

kill.ui: IAM console > Users > user > Security credentials > Access keys > Actions > Deactivate, then Delete; add an inline deny policy on the user to cut off temporary credentials already minted
kill.cli: aws iam update-access-key --status Inactive; aws iam delete-access-key; aws iam put-user-policy

offboard.ui: IAM console > Users > select user > Delete (deactivate active access keys first)
offboard.cli: aws iam delete-user (after removing keys, policies, groups)

token_format.notes: Access key ID AKIA...; 40-char secret not logged.

log_sources.name: AWS CloudTrail event history
log_sources.notes: On by default; 90 days of management events per Region; free. Data events (e.g. S3 GetObject) not included.

log_sources.name: CloudTrail trail / event data store
log_sources.notes: Needed for retention beyond 90 days; data events off by default and cost extra.

log_sources.name: IAM credential report / GetAccessKeyLastUsed
log_sources.notes: Last-used date, service, Region; first use per 15 min only.

credential_id_fields.notes: Key ID used to sign the request; may be empty for security reasons.

lifecycle_events.notes: IAM API action; CloudTrail logs all IAM calls.

anomaly_cues: GetCallerIdentity from a new IP or user agent
Key used after long idle period (credential report)

containment.steps: UpdateAccessKey Status=Inactive, then DeleteAccessKey. Also attach aws:TokenIssueTime deny to the user to block STS sessions the key may have minted.
containment.notes: Deactivation stops the key immediately, but temporary credentials already obtained with it (GetSessionToken/AssumeRole) stay valid until expiry unless permissions are also changed.

calls.log_notes: All STS calls logged as management events; cannot be denied by policy.

calls.reveals: All IAM users, groups, roles, policies
All buckets owned by the account
calls.log_notes: Management/data classification not verified on fetched pages.
S3 object-level data event; only logged if data events are enabled on a trail (extra cost).

detections.title: AWS User API Key Created
detections.detects: An IAM user access key was created by a different principal than the key owner.

detections.title: AWS IAM Backdoor Users Keys
detections.detects: CreateAccessKey where the caller is not the user receiving the key.

detections.title: New IAM Credentials Updated
detections.detects: Successful creation of access keys, users, or login profiles, or password changes.

detections.title: AWS IAM S3Browser User or AccessKey Creation
detections.detects: IAM user or access key creation from the S3 Browser user agent.

detections.title: AWS IAM Access Key Compromise Detection
detections.detects: AWS attached an exposed-credential quarantine policy to a user whose access key was found leaked.

detections.title: AWS Compromised IAM Key Quarantine
detections.detects: The AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantineV2 managed policy was attached to a user, group, or role.

detections.title: AWS.CloudTrail.UserAccessKeyAuth
detections.detects: Any successful API call made with a long-term IAM user access key (key ID starting with AKIA).

detections.title: AWS STS GetSessionToken by IAM User
detections.detects: An IAM user called GetSessionToken to turn long-term keys into temporary credentials.

detections.title: AWS STS GetSessionToken Misuse
detections.detects: GetSessionToken called by an IAM user.

detections.title: AWS STS GetCallerIdentity via TruffleHog
detections.detects: GetCallerIdentity with a TruffleHog user agent, used to check whether leaked access keys still work.

detections.title: AWS STS GetCallerIdentity Enumeration Via TruffleHog
detections.detects: GetCallerIdentity with a TruffleHog user agent.

detections.title: PUA - AWS TruffleHog Execution
detections.detects: Any CloudTrail event with the TruffleHog user agent.

detections.title: Detect Reconnaissance from IAM Users
detections.detects: An IAM user hit AccessDenied on List/Describe/Get calls in common services, a sign of a stolen key being used for recon.

detections.title: AWS Console GetSigninToken Potential Abuse
detections.detects: GetSigninToken from a non-SSO user agent, used to turn CLI credentials into a console session.

detections.title: AWS Console GetSigninToken Potential Abuse
detections.detects: GetSigninToken from a user agent other than the console federation endpoint.
